newsitem.title: FRANCE: Legras sees EU grain crop at 193-194 million tns.
newsitem.headline: Legras sees EU grain crop at 193-194 million tns.

text.p: A senior European Union farm official on Wednesday predicted a record EU grain harvest of 193-194 million tonnes this year -- nearly 20 million tonnes above last year's crop but below estimates of 200 million tonnes also circulating within the EU.

Guy Legras, the European Commission's director general for agriculture, told Reuters in an interview this year's grain harvest looked like a record, but for now he regarded 200 million tonnes as too high.
He also provisionally predicted a 1996 soft wheat harvest of 86-87 million tonnes, up from 79.5 million tonnes in 1995.
EU figures obtained in Brussels on Wednesday pointed to a grain crop of 200.7 million tonnes, up 23 million from 1995.
Legras did not refer to this document but said he personally thought projections of 200 million tonnes were "not serious."
It was not clear whether the higher estimates were based on projections by EU member states, which the Commission often suspects of inflating their individual supply targets.
A European Commission grain official in Brussels cautioned that the figures were only a preliminary estimate and were subject to revision.
-- Paule Bonjean, Tim Hepher, Paris newsroom +331 4221 5146
